title: Dynamic programming
objective: Build an answer from smaller answers stored in a table, so nothing is worked out twice.

sources.title: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. (MIT Press, 2022): dynamic programming
Laaksonen, Competitive Programmer's Handbook: dynamic programming: the coin problem

simplifies: The table here is filled bottom-up. The same answers can be found top-down with recursion plus a cache (memoisation); both avoid repeating work.

quiz.prompt: Coins {1, 3, 4}, amount 6. Biggest-coin-first gives 4 + 1 + 1. What is the fewest?

options.explanation: Right. Greedy grabs the 4 and gets stuck; the table tries every last coin for every amount.
That is the greedy answer, but 3 + 3 uses fewer coins.
That works, but it is the most coins, not the fewest.

quiz.prompt: Why is d[a] built from smaller amounts like d[a − 3]?

options.text: The last coin used was some coin c, and the rest is the best way to make a − c, already in the table
options.explanation: Right. Every answer reuses answers to smaller problems: that is dynamic programming.
Order matters only so the smaller answers exist first.
Nothing is guessed: each entry is the best over all possible last coins.
